Compiled cleanly with `-Wall -Werror` and all tests passed. Here's what `ringbuf.c` implements:

| Function | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `rb_create` / `rb_destroy` | Allocate/free storage; `destroy(NULL)` is a no-op |
| `rb_size` / `rb_capacity` | Return current used slots and fixed capacity |
| `rb_clear` | Reset head/tail/count to zero |
| `rb_write` | Store up to `len` bytes, wrapping at capacity boundary; truncates if more data is offered than fits |
| `rb_read` | Remove oldest bytes first, wrapping at boundary |
| `rb_peek` | Same as read but leaves `count` untouched |

The struct definition lives in `ringbuf.c` so the header keeps the internal representation opaque. All null-pointer inputs are handled defensively (return 0 for queries, no-op for destroy/clear).
Cleaned up the test binary. The implementation is complete in `ringbuf.c`, with `test.c` containing the self-check tests.
